findings.issue: The new mask replaces ` *\b<duration>` with a fixed ` <duration>`, so it swallows the whole run of spaces between the exit code and the duration as well as the digit-dependent padding. A change to the step line's column layout that only a present-but-empty executor.phaseGateOnly caused (the gap between `exit N` and the duration) is no longer visible to pgo7. Measured in a scratch copy: a runner that, only when the key is present, widens that gap (`exit 0  ` -> `exit 0     `) is FAIL under the old mask and PASS under the new one. The class pgo7 exists for (the setting changing what the runner prints) is still caught for an extra line, a reworded banner, a renamed step, a changed check-count text and a changed duration unit; only pure whitespace layout inside the swallowed gap is lost.
findings.resolution: Keep the layout invariant instead of dropping it: the width of (padding + duration text) is constant for one exit-code width, so substitute with a function that returns `"<duration>".rjust(len(match.group(0)))` (or equivalent) rather than a fixed ' <duration>'. The digit-count-dependent padding then still collapses to one spelling while a real column-width change still reddens the case.

preExisting.issue: The final `re.sub(r"\d+", "N", text)` hides any difference that is only in digits, before and after this diff: a runner that prints `exit 7` instead of `exit 0` on the step line (or a different check count) only when the setting is empty leaves the masked texts equal. Measured: that mutation SURVIVES under both the old and the new mask; pgo7 only compares the exit code of the run, the step names and the row keys besides the text.
preExisting.resolution: Not charged to this task. If pgo7 should see digit-only differences, mask only the named variable fields (duration, ids, stamps) and leave the other digits as they are.

intent.note: Task clause 1 ('make the case's failure say what differed ... the first differing pair of lines (and the lengths if they differ)'): _first_line_difference is appended to pgo7's label and prints 'line K differs: <a> / <b>' plus both counts when they differ; in my scratch runs it named the pair (e.g. "line 11 differs: 'GATE GREEN: sweep, browser, tree unchanged' / 'GATE GREEN (empty): ...'" and "line 1 differs ... (12 line(s) against 13)"). Clause 2/3 ('the mask must cover its whole varying part'): the step line is '  %-12s exit %-3d %10s  %s' (run-test-gate.py:5047), so the duration is right-aligned and its padding encodes its digit count; the old mask kept that padding. The new mask covers it, and it covers every form _fmt.human_duration prints (ms, N.N s, N m NN s): I rendered 26 values from 0 ms to 7 h, including 999/1000, 59949/59950/59999, 60000 and 3600000, through the mask and got one single masked line; '(not timed)' and '(repeated)' lines carry no duration and are untouched. The new regex only removes text the old digit collapse would have left padded, so no form the old mask covered is now missed; the one thing lost is whitespace layout inside the swallowed gap (finding 1). The cause is stated as reproduced under load (old mask red 18 of 64, fixed mask 0 of 64) and, honestly, not observed line by line in the CI log; that meets acceptance 2's 'evidence or not established with what was ruled out'. The executor's claim describes the diff: one file changed, runner untouched, _pgo_masked has the one caller pgo7 (the dependants it lists are not touched).
